Definition
[kappa noncollapsing] Source: kleiner-lott 1. Definition 38.1\group Kleiner–Lott Kappa Solutions

Given $\kappa >0$, a $\kappa $-solution is a Ricci flow on $(-\infty ,C)$ or $(-\infty ,C]$ with complete time slices, curvature bounded on compact time intervals, nonnegative curvature operator, $R>0$, and $\kappa $-noncollapsing at all scales. The term may also refer to a solution with this property for some $\kappa >0$. For ancient solutions $R_t\geq 0$, so the two standard noncollapsing definitions are equivalent up to changing $\kappa $ by distance distortion. Finite-time blowup limits on compact manifolds are $\kappa $-solutions.
